interpretation: The observed 2 km negative to 5 km positive sign switch is not itself unusual under the frozen block-preserving null; approximately one quarter of null permutations show that direction switch.
The joint event of the observed switch direction plus a 5 km minus 2 km contrast at least as large as observed occurs with plus-one probability 0.0810, above the frozen 0.05 interpretation threshold.
Therefore the 1/2/5 km sensitivity cannot be promoted to an ecological discovery of scale dependence.
The correct wording is that the apparent interaction is sensitive to radius and that the observed cross-radius instability is compatible with finite-sample/block-permutation fluctuation.
The frozen 2 km analysis remains primary, but the lack of cross-radius stability is an important limitation.
